**Perfect separation lets likelihood improve forever by increasing confidence.** Suppose a vector w gives every training example a positive signed margin $y_iw^Tx_i$, with labels encoded as -1 and +1. Multiplying w by c preserves all classifications while pushing predicted probabilities closer to the observed zero/one labels. [1](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/linear_model.html)

Each logistic loss term is $\log(1+e^{-c y_iw^Tx_i})$. Since every signed margin is positive, every term approaches zero as c grows. For any finite c, a larger value improves the objective. There is an infimum but no finite unregularized solution attaining it under complete separation.

**Classification accuracy can therefore hide estimation failure.** Accuracy is already 100%, yet coefficients continue growing. A numerical solver may stop because of tolerances or overflow, not because the finite maximum-likelihood estimate exists. Very large coefficients in a small dataset can reflect separation rather than strong, precisely estimated effects.

An L2 penalty grows quadratically with coefficient magnitude, balancing the decreasing data loss and producing a finite optimum in penalized directions. Check intercept treatment and one-class degeneracies as well. Regularization controls the confidence and coefficient scale; it does not prove the separating pattern will generalize to new observations.

**Technical details and references.**

If a separating direction makes every signed margin positive, multiplying its weights by larger constants drives all training probabilities toward correct extremes and log loss toward zero. No finite unregularized maximum-likelihood solution is attained under complete separation. [1](https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/linear_model.html)

$$L(cw)=\sum_i\log(1+e^{-c y_iw^Tx_i})\to0\quad(c\to\infty).$$

Numerical solvers may report huge coefficients, warnings, or an apparent converged value caused by finite precision. An L2 penalty grows quadratically with scale, producing a finite optimum for penalized directions. Intercept handling and degenerate all-one-class data still need care. Use regularization, inspect separation and sample size, and do not interpret enormous coefficients as precise evidence of an enormous causal effect.
